key_insight: High-rate cavitation can reveal effective viscosity and shear modulus reductions that occur at different stages, challenging constant-property assumptions.
engineering_relevance: Tracking property changes during rapid deformation can improve characterization of soft, tissue-like materials for biomechanics and medical engineering.
method: Infer viscoelastic properties from laser-induced cavitation bubble radius–time histories using Inertial Microcavitation Rheometry.
Represent evolving shear modulus, viscosity, or both with normalized sigmoid histories.
Evaluate recovery on synthetic histories and apply the framework to polyacrylamide and gelatin datasets.
evidence_signal: Synthetic tests recovered prescribed constant and evolving histories; experimental datasets showed viscosity decreases throughout, while shear modulus reductions varied by material and formulation.
watch_item: Inferred histories are effective properties constrained by sigmoid evolution and do not by themselves distinguish damage, fracture, and plasticity.
paper_title: Soft material mechanical property degradation at high strain rates
